# Issues
- vague direction
- unformatted output
- missing examples
- limited evaluation
- no task division

::: {.notes}
These issues and the following principles are taken from @Phoenix2024, Chapter 1. Note that the authors assert that they are not *tips* or *hacks* but model-agnostic principles.
:::

# Principles arising from the issues
- give direction
- specify format
- provide examples
- evaluate quality
- divide labor

## 1. Give direction
- imagine direction a human would need
- ask it to role-play (e.g., Steve Jobs product-naming)
- ask it to generate a list of best practices, then ask it to follow them
- for image generation, supply the name of a prominent artist

::: {.notes}
Several names are given to the practice of asking it to supply best practices and then follow those best practices. Generated knowledge prompting (@Liu2022), prewarming, and internal retrieval are the best known.
:::

## 2. Specify format
- JSON, YAML, HTML are all worthwhile formats to specify---JSON because it is universally used in web applications, YAML as an occasional substitute for JSON, and HTML because it can be directly pasted into a document
- stock photo, illustration, and oil painting are common image generation formats to specify, but there are many more
- specifications may clash in unpredictable ways, so it may be necessary to drop some specifications during prompt development
- there may also be clashes between principles 1 and 2, leading you to sacrifice one or the other

::: {.notes}
At a minimum, all knowledge workers should know JSON, HTML, and CSS for communication online. If you aren't familiar with JSON, you should immediately familiarize yourself with it. @Phoenix2024 recommends the [W3Schools tutorial](https://www.w3schools.com/js/js_json_intro.asp). I can't stand the ads on that site, so I prefer [https://json.org](https://json.org). But there you need to understand rail diagrams.
:::

## 3. Provide examples
- zero-shot prompts contain *no* examples
- one-shot prompts contain *one* example
- few-shot prompts contain *several* examples
